scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: First-order Markov: the current class depends only on the previous one, which already summarizes earlier history

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: each circle is a class and arrow numbers are transition probabilities; the right unrolls time, thick arrows are direct dependence, crossed gray dashed lines are dependence blocked by the assumption.

scene-u01-pnew1-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew1-41.text: The three numbers leaving each node sum to $1$ (each row sums to $1$)

scene-u01-pnew1-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew1-43.text: Unrolled in time: only thick arrows are direct dependence

scene-u01-pnew1-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew1-69.text: "Earlier history does not matter" is wrong: it still acts through the previous class; the assumption only says that, given the previous class, earlier classes add no new information.

scene-u01-pnew1-70.name: text#70
scene-u01-pnew1-70.text: Thick arrows: one-step transitions; gray dashed: direct dependence blocked by the assumption

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: top left is the two-class transition table, top right multiplies each step of two paths; bottom left shows how the last chain-rule term simplifies, bottom right is the sequence objective.

scene-u01-pnew2-62.name: text#62
scene-u01-pnew2-62.text: Each step multiplies one transition; the switching path (bottom) multiplies two factors of $0.1$, so it is small
